sand.measured: Tjusta's raked bunkers are tan, not white: on the 2025-06-14 photo seven bunkers (11, 13 twice, 7, the meadow on 7, 18 and the range green) read brightness 137-169, NDVI -0.20 to -0.25, warmth 18-26, against turf at brightness 98-110 and NDVI +0.08 to +0.24 and gravel at about 90.

fairways.why: OSM has six fairways here, drawn in 2012, so the turf model learned that every other hole's fairway was rough: on one photo it found 2,000 m2 of fairway on the 505 m 7th. Each flight's model is taught from the holes' own lines instead, and the fairway is what three flights agree on: pale in the June 2025 drought, mown in May 2023, striped in April 2021. No single flight separates it from the semi-rough (on the line ground one flight gets 60-90% right and 38-90% of the rough). The July 2019 flight added nothing and is left out. Hole 4's line carries over trees and is left out of the teaching.
fairways.fitWhy: Fairway against rough, taught from hole lines on these photos, does not settle in the tracer's fixed 900 steps: on the 2023 flight the loss bounced between 0.5 and 1.3 and the model's fairway accuracy between 0.61 and 0.92 from one checkpoint to the next, and three hole lines moved 2 m took a quarter off the 18th fairway. Fitted to convergence, three samples of the same labels give 0.817-0.823 and disagree on 0.9% of the 55 m corridor.
fairways.holeReachWhy: The holes lie side by side in open ground (1, 5, 17 and 18; 7 and 15; 8 and 14), where their mown turf is one connected piece: each piece of it goes to the hole whose line is nearest, and none beyond 55 m of a line, which leaves the range and the farm's lawns out.
